1.explanation: BpmnConnectSnapping.js contains the logic for snapping connections during message‐flow creation, but currently only snaps to BPMN Events (not to generic participant boundaries), so internal lane boundaries aren’t offered as drop targets. BpmnSnappingUtil.js defines getBoundaryAttachment helper logic for snapping to arbitrary element borders, but it’s never used for message flows. Finally, BpmnRules.js implements the canConnectMessageFlow rule that determines where message flows may start and end; its message flow target logic needs to account for single‐lane pools (participants) and allow connections anywhere on the pool boundary, not only on the header. These three files together must be updated so that message flows can snap to and be permitted on the full pool boundary inside a lane.
1.bug_scenario: After creating two pools and connecting them with a message flow (by clicking in each pool’s interior), adding and immediately removing a second lane from one pool erroneously changes where you can anchor the message flow on that pool. Instead of being able to drop the connector anywhere inside the single remaining lane, you can only drop it on the pool’s header bar. In other words, the pool boundary inside the lane no longer acts as a valid target for the message flow after a transient second lane.
